name: showreel-24-sticky

voice.text: Why did your sticky header stop sticking? A parent has overflow hidden. That makes it a scroll box, so the header sticks inside it and scrolls away. The fix: overflow, clip. It clips, but isn't a scroll box. Now the header stays on top.

caption:
Why did your sticky header stop sticking? 📌

A sticky element sticks to its nearest ancestor with a scrolling mechanism, and overflow: hidden creates one even if that box never scrolls (MDN). So one wrapper with overflow: hidden captures your header, and it scrolls away with the page. Swap it for overflow: clip: the content is still clipped, but the box is not a scroll container, so the header sticks to the page again. Chrome 90+, Firefox 81+, Safari 16+. (No top value set? Sticky never sticks; check that first.)
Save it for the next time a header won't stick, or send it to whoever builds your site.

sources.note: MDN position: a sticky element sticks to its nearest ancestor that has a scrolling mechanism (created when overflow is hidden, scroll, auto, or overlay), even if that ancestor isn't the nearest actually scrolling ancestor; it needs a non-auto inset such as top
MDN overflow: hidden clips and the box is a scroll container; clip clips at the overflow clip edge and the box is not a scroll container
overflow: clip: Chrome 90, Firefox 81, Safari 16 (Edge follows Chrome)
